title: A Machine for the Signal
premise: Noor Kavanagh, a clone who inherited both the original's unsolved murder and her debts, pilots a cargo hauler along the silent relay route between the breakaway colonies and a Earth that has stopped answering. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, Noor's ship is thrown into the path of a derelict transmitter carrying the last Earth transmission loop — and a message that proves the original Noor was killed for finding it. Hunted by colony zealots who need the war to continue, Noor must decode and deliver the message before the loop decays, discovering that the original chose to die rather than send it. In the end, Noor broadcasts the truth anyway, ending the war but erasing the last claim to the original's identity — and chooses, finally, to be someone new.
about_author: Kestrel Ravensworth is a former radio astronomer who spent six years listening to dead frequencies before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station on the Atlantic coast, where the static never quite stops.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Running the long route with a half-broken crew and a dead woman's name, Noor survives the nine-second gravity flicker and finds a derelict transmitter embedded in their path — still looping. Inside its logs, the original Noor's voice. The emotional beat is dread laced with recognition: the dead self left a message, and someone wanted it buried.

chapters.title: The Loop That Won't Die
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and crew engineer Sef's POV. Decoding the transmission reveals the war began on a lie Earth manufactured to keep the colonies dependent — and that the original Noor died protecting this proof. Colony zealots board at the mid-route station, hunting the ship. The emotional beat is betrayal curdling into resolve: Noor stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: What the Original Chose
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, intercut with recovered memory-logs of the original's final days. Cornered at the last relay, Noor discovers the original refused to send the message because its truth would also doom the colonies' fledgling independence. The zealots breach the hull; Sef is lost holding the airlock. Climax beat: Noor must decide whether the dead self's silence was cowardice — or mercy.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, final transmission loop decaying in real time. Noor overrides the original's last command and sends everything — the lie, the murder, the cost — letting both sides hear the war end in their own voices. Earth's loop goes silent for good; the colonies, furious and free, let the hauler pass. The emotional beat is grief becoming authorship: Noor deletes the original's identity file and signs the log as themselves.
